# @arki/live

> Live queries on your own Postgres: procedures declare the tables they read in oRPC contract meta, a statement trigger publishes a hint at commit, and a hub feeds one stream per tab so clients refetch what a commit touched. A table scoped by a tenant key hints its changed keys too, and a client gets only its granted keys. Only table names and keys travel.

## Import paths
- `@arki/live`: the portable core. `createLiveHub` (`hub.cursor()` for server rendering, `hub.open({ view })`, `hub.onChange` for server-side watchers only), `liveReceipts` (HMAC receipts instead of raw txids), `createLiveClient` (the stream reader with reconnects), `live` (meta from tags), `affectedPaths`, `liveTables`, `parseLiveEvent` and `parseLiveCursor` (shape checks for what arrives from outside; cursors are opaque), `LIVE_ERROR_CODES` and the plain types.
- `@arki/live/drizzle`: `live` (meta from Drizzle tables, `scope: { org: 'input.orgId' | 'session' }`), `liveScopes` (which tables are scoped, by which NOT NULL key column), `tableTag`, `snapshot` (one read-only repeatable-read transaction per call).
- `@arki/live/orpc`: `liveRead`, the middleware that runs a live procedure inside one snapshot; `liveManifest`, the live procedures of a contract.
- `@arki/live/http`: `liveEndpoint`, the `GET /api/live` SSE stream (400/401/503 before headers, grant → view with keys per dimension, `reauthorize` tables, `bye` at `maxAgeMs`).
- `@arki/live/dot`: `liveQueries`, the Dot plugin: trigger check at boot (E002), `LISTEN` at start, publishes `live` and `liveRoutes`.
- `@arki/live/pg`: `liveMigration` (the trigger SQL), `liveChannel`, `verifyLiveTriggers` (the boot check), `touch` (publish a tag by hand), `pgSource` (the hub's source on a `pg` pool).
- `@arki/live/react`: `LiveProvider` (one stream per tab), `useLiveQuery(orpc.x.queryOptions({ input }))`, `useLiveStatus`, `setLiveCursor` (dehydrate the hub cursor), `awaitTxId(queryClient, receipt)` (the mutation returns `receipts.of(txid)`).
- `@arki/live/testing`: `fakeSource`, a source a test drives; `waitForInvalidation(queryClient, path)`.

## Rules that bite
- Declare every table a live procedure reads. An undeclared table never refetches.
- Inside a `liveRead` handler read only through `context.liveRead`. The root `db` is a second snapshot.
- `snapshot()` takes the root database, never a `tx`: a nested transaction is a savepoint.
- Type the `liveRead` select with the handler context (`{ db, repos }`), not `Deps`: an `entrypointOnly` db is not in `Deps`.
- Never declare `live()` on a per-request table (sessions, counters): it refetches constantly. Do declare auth tables the answer depends on (memberships, roles).
- Never parse a cursor: it is sealed. Send it back as received.
- No `initialData` on a live query (a type error); use `placeholderData`.
- Server rendering: `setLiveCursor(queryClient, await hub.cursor())` before the page's data is read, never after.
- Account switch: `queryClient.resetQueries()` and remount `<LiveProvider key={userId}>`; the old stream keeps the old grant until `maxAgeMs`.
- A cursor resumes only by its age (`replayMs`). The `replayEnvelopes` and `replayBytes` caps are overloads: a new epoch, every client resets.
- Frames carry receipts, never raw txids: `createLiveHub({ receipts: liveReceipts({ app, secret }) })`, the secret from app config (32+ characters, `openssl rand -base64 32`). A mutation returns `receipts.of(txid)`; never the txid itself.
- The grant becomes a view in the hub (`hub.open({ view })`) and applies before each stream's window and queue. Never filter hints after them: a hidden write would change the stream's timing or cause its `bye`.
- Scoped table: grant keys per dimension (`{ scopes: { org: orgIds } }` or `'all'`); a dimension left out shows nothing. A procedure reading it declares `scope`, else it is live only for `'all'` grants. Scope by `user` when org members must not see each other's activity.
- Never give a trigger function rights its caller lacks: any role that can connect may LISTEN on any channel. TRUNCATE under row-level security resets every client instead of publishing keys.
